summary: Round 1 had no findings, so nothing carried over. In src, the only changes since round 1 (a24bba9..9859cf6) are type signatures: recommend, recommendPostflop and gradeView now declare `O extends object`, and ExactOptions<O, Allowed> = O & Allowed & Record<extra keys, never>. No function bodies, imports or runtime values changed, so runtime behaviour is unchanged (the emitted JS is the same). REQ-035.3 is stronger. Before, an options variable with only bot-only keys (e.g. { style }) could get past the guard. Now the `& Allowed` term means the argument must be assignable to the allowed options, and every extra key is typed never. New @ts-expect-error tests in tests/advice/ranges.test.ts cover a style-only variable and a random-source variable for all three entry points. Running `tsc --noEmit` passes, so those expectations hold. Every bot call site (rock, maniac, tag, calling-station) still passes adviceOptions(options) or a spread of it, and adviceOptions copies only equity, chart and opponentRanges. The documented gaps (an explicit type argument, or a variable already widened to RecommendOptions) are compile-time only. They are also covered by the runtime copy in adviceOptions and by the import boundaries. The worker boundary (advice-service.ts) and the review path are unchanged. No new dependencies, I/O, randomness or secrets.
